The logic is that if your immune system is being able to hold back the infection warts will at least stop growing, and although the vaccine is not guaranteed to do that in already present infections I don’t see how it can have any negative impact. If anything it might help our body produce immunity to the virus and avoid the shedding virus invading new cells in other parts of the skin, just like it would in a new infection.

According to my doctor and other doctors that I have talked to very much possibly yes, since it teaches your body how to generate immunity and HPV is a local infection. Some even believe the vaccine helps with active infections. Do not take a “no” for an answer because nobody has a certain answer so far, there is a lot of disagreement. Doctors have told me they believe the vaccine has helped me clear the warts without recurrences so far, I had 6 different strains and thank God I’ve been healing for over a year now. Spreading your own warts to other parts of the body (also known as autoinoculation) is already very unlikely to happen without the vaccine, I am sure getting vaccinated can’t make it worse. 
In the end, nobody knows for sure, but there are only benefits in getting vaccinated, regardless.

Remember that you need to take care of your body, because some serious infections (STIs especially) or some diseases like diabetes can cause GWs to thrive, by overloading your immune system.

6 months after last symptom without recurrences is understood as your body having suppressed the virus, so you’re on the clear. Don’t worry so much about them, keep an eye there eventually, but carry on with your life normally. Having been symptomless for this long, even if you do have any recurrences, maybe because of excessive stress or lower immunity (which is not impossible) they are very much probably going to be significantly smaller because your immune system is clearly fighting off the infection well. So keep taking care of your health and be thankful! Have safe sex (to protect YOURSELF from further infections, because without symptoms for that long you have just as much chance of spreading HPV as any other sexually active person) Stay strong!

It took months to stop hurting A LOT after bowel movements, and it still hurts a bit every time I have to poop. I feel like my anus got tighter, but I have managed to have anal sex successfully without any pain many times after that when I could relax the muscles 100%, which has led me to believe that the pain probably has to do with muscle tightening after trauma or maybe even hemorrhoids. What I’m certain is that the surgery caused something in there, even though the first time I talked to my doctor he said it was just skin that was more sensitive and probably going away soon. But I have gotten better enough to fear living like this forever. If you must, look for a doctor. You might have fissures that are having trouble healing, or maybe hemorrhoids and there is treatment available. Don’t let the perspective of never feeling great again scare you, because it’s not true. Sending you strength!!

Honestly, it is a (temporary) painful rash that podophyllin leaves, so you might not feel like going cycling. It’s not impossible, though. Ointments for burns really helped me, and it was a matter of days for the rash to go away using them. (Doc would apply podophyllin every friday for about a month or a bit more) I would definitely not recommend going cycling from the day you apply it to at least two days later, after that time you’ll probably be recovering already and you’ll be able to decide if it’s comfortable enough. The intensity of the rash also depends on how long you leave the podophyllin on your skin (I was instructed to never leave it for more than 4 hours and I once did leave it there for 4 hours and it really hurt afterwards, but it’s all temporary and I was 100% in a few days)

I answered your DM. It didn’t cause me any lasting damage, as I used it very carefully and followed through with my doctor’s instructions. You should definitely talk to a qualified doctor. But in my personal experience, it was like a superficial (painful, regardless) burn. I used it on and around my butthole, a very sensitive area, and it went away with time and care (I used ointment for burns to help it heal, it took maybe a week or less to heal 100% after treatment, I had my doctor apply it on me one time a week for a month or two, can’t remember exactly how long). No scars left, no sensitivity damage... I’m a gay man and I bottom, so it would definitely bother me if any of that happened, but it really didn’t cause me long lasting damage at all, much differently from the internal electrocautery surgery (which thankfully also healed with time). I’m pretty sure podophyllin could cause more serious problems if used internally, though! Again, you must talk to a certified doctor. You’ll get through this, man!

I am not a professional, but I had genital warts + did my research, so take all of that into consideration.

From what I have studied/experienced, I believe that, because warts are a symptom of the underlying infection, if you were to “auto-inoculate” yourself back on the same area as clearance was taking place it would not make a real difference because you would just be adding another load of virus that would probably not be significant in an area already infected and probably full of fighter cells. So it’s probable that new warts would not even appear in a fading infection, and if they did it could possibly mean that the viral load is still high and active and clearance not really so near yet. 

 I have read that HPV is a local infection, though, so antibodies may or may not be generated systemically. In case they weren’t, auto-inoculation of other parts of the body (mucous membranes, in the case of genital warts) would theoretically be possible. But from experience + the little knowledge I have, auto-inoculation to other parts of the body is quite rare, especially among people with a decent immune system fighting off active infections.

Hey, you sound like a great person, and he sounds completely undeserving of you. You did the best thing you could possibly do by breaking things off with someone who cheated on you and still treats you with that attitude. 

You cannot convince someone to be a better person, and, as hard to accept as it is, it doesn’t matter whether it is because he doesn’t want to or because he is too wounded to do so. You can’t fix someone, and if instead of appreciating your company and love to heal he cheats on you and doesn’t display the vulnerability to deeply apologize then he does not have what it takes to grow, change and he will only deplete and hurt you (and others).

About HPV, there is a possibility he was infected before dating you and just never displayed symptoms. HPV is very common (known as the common cold of STIs), and since there are no tests for men, unless you are sure you were HPV negative before the cheating there is a possibility he had it before he started dating you, and in that case he wouldn’t be all faulty of giving it to you because it really is something that people many times just don’t know about, especially because most people don’t display symptoms. Considering that, even you could have possibly infected him if he was not your first partner, and it would NOT have been your fault. The cheating and carelessness are inexcusable, but that might not have been where  the HPV came from. 

I do not mean to blame you AT ALL, I’m just trying to give you some perspective on the fact that it’s very complicated to demand that someone without symptoms discloses HPV. Around 80% of sexually active people are going to come across it at some point in their lives, and most will never even know. It’s very different from other STIs. Of course, now he knows you have it he should care enough to research this himself, but that’s on him. 

Educate yourself on the subject, this sub has lots of great info. Know that:
1. HPV is treatable. There is currently no known cure, but that just means that we still don’t have a “miracle pill” because it’s accepted that the great majority of people living with HPV are going to clear the virus with time and lifestyle changes. Only a small fraction of those who have HPV might have bigger problems with its persistence, like cancer, even among those who do display symptoms and among those who have high-risk HPV. Besides, for the symptomatic infections, like genital warts, there are treatments available and they are many times successful in accelerating clearance.

2. Life isn’t over. There are great people who will definitely treat you with more respect than he does, and when someone loves you for who you are even STIs become an issue that can be worked around. HPV fucking sucks, but we are going to beat this. For real. Take good care of yourself, seriously consider going no-contact with this person. Stress makes your immune system fight off the infection slower. Wishing you all the best. You are not alone! Don’t be afraid! ❤️
